cues.text: A tag is how a garment finds its way back to the right customer. Every piece gets a tag, and the tag goes in the right place.
The golden rule: the staple or pin goes through the label, not the fabric.
A staple through the fabric leaves holes, snags, and runs that cannot be fixed.
Shirts: the label inside the back of the collar, or the care label on the side seam.
Pants and skirts: the label inside the back of the waistband.
Jackets and suits: the brand label inside the neck. A suit has two pieces, so the jacket and the pants each get a tag with the same number.
Sweaters and knits: use a safety pin on the care label. Staples pull the knit threads.
Dresses, silk, and delicate pieces: a safety pin through the label is the gentle choice.
Ties: through the small label on the back of the tie.
No label? Use a safety pin through an inside seam, where it cannot be seen.
Or loop the tag onto a belt loop or a button. Never put a tag on the outside of the garment.
Before you move on, check every tag. The number is clear and matches the ticket.
Every piece has its own tag. Tug gently to make sure it stays on.
